risks.note: MD&A Risks & Concerns: operations are closely linked to defence procurement timelines, naval project execution schedules and government spending priorities, and delays in approvals, project execution or procurement cycles may impact order inflows and revenue recognition. Mitigation cited is strengthening long-term relationships within the defence ecosystem while expanding execution capabilities across specialised naval applications - it does not reduce the underlying single-customer-ecosystem dependence.

Board risk table flags 'Strategic Sector Shifts' - rapid changes in Indian Defence procurement policies or technical specifications for naval platforms - which can strand qualification work in a business where approval cycles are long. Mitigation is active R&D and closer collaboration with defence laboratories to stay aligned.
risks.risk: Rapid shifts in Indian defence procurement policy and naval technical specifications

risks.note: MD&A: the industry continues to experience volatility in refrigerant prices driven by global supply-and-demand imbalances, and supply chain disruptions and component shortages can directly impact procurement timelines and project deliveries - i.e. it hits both margin and delivery schedules. Mitigation is diversified sourcing, strategic vendor partnerships and calibrated inventory planning.
risks.risk: Volatile refrigerant pricing and component supply-chain pressure

risks.note: Board risk table rates 'Supply Chain Continuity' as High priority: reliance on specialized raw materials such as high-grade alloys or electronic controllers can lead to production delays. Mitigation is developing an alternate vendor base and increasing in-house fabrication of critical components to reduce dependency on imports and logistical issues.
risks.risk: Reliance on specialised imported raw materials for production continuity

risks.note: MD&A: defence-grade cooling systems for defence, marine and data centre applications involve high-order technical complexity, but availability of specialised talent in system design, advanced controls and precision installation remains limited; this talent gap can impact project timelines, service quality and the scalability of operations - a direct constraint on the company's stated capacity expansion.

The statutory auditor designated 'Valuation of Inventory' a Key Audit Matter, noting inventory forms a significant part of the assets at Rs. 5,477.04 lacs as of 31st March 2026, representing 18.26% of total assets, made up of raw materials, spares and semi-finished goods including steel, pumps and spares managed internally at warehouse. The judgement inherent in valuing that block is a recurring audit-attention item for a project-execution business.
risks.risk: Inventory carrying value and working-capital intensity

risks.note: The auditor's report carries an Emphasis of Matter drawing attention to the Company's listing on the SME Platform of BSE Limited on 1st August 2025, the consequent changes in share capital structure and the utilisation of IPO proceeds towards the objects of the issue (opinion not modified). FY26 capex was part-funded from those IPO proceeds, so utilisation against stated objects remains a live monitoring item in the company's first year as a listed entity.
risks.risk: Newly listed SME: IPO proceeds utilisation and reduced governance-disclosure regime
